artworks.title: Eurus (Tower of the Winds, Athens)
artworks.description: Southeast face of the Horologion of Andronikos in the Roman Agora: the relief of Eurus (Euros), the east-southeast wind, cloaked and bringing rain. The eight Anemoi of the Tower of the Winds remain the east wind's most famous ancient image in stone.

artworks.title: Eurus
artworks.description: Wood engraving from August Heinrich Petiscus' Der Olymp (Leipzig, 1878): Eurus as the personified east wind of autumn — cloak, seasonal attributes, and the classical schoolbook image of the Anemos who brings changeable weather from the sunrise.

artworks.title: Eurus (Virginia Museum of Fine Arts)
artworks.description: Relief image of Eurus in the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts (Richmond 51.13): the east wind as a winged or cloaked Anemos, one of the four cardinal winds who also stand for the seasons in later allegory.

music.title: Il pomo d'oro
music.description: Cesti's Viennese festa teatrale for Leopold I peopled the stage with Olympians and winds — Eurus among the mythic machinery of Baroque spectacle.

popCulture.title: Eurus
popCulture.description: Greek east wind, son of Astraeus and Eos — counterpart of Latin Vulturnus/Eurus, and one face of the Tower of the Winds.
